moduleTitle: Computer Networking & How the Internet Works
title: IP Addresses, DNS, TCP/IP & HTTP Request-Response Cycle
plainExplanation: When you type a website name into your browser, it is just like mailing a letter. DNS is the phonebook that translates a human name (like example.com) into a numbered street address (IP address). TCP splits your message into numbered packets so nothing gets lost, and HTTP is the polite language browsers and servers speak to ask for pages and send back replies.
whyItMatters: Every web app, mobile app, cloud server, and AI API communicates over networks. Knowing DNS, HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE), and status codes (200, 401, 404, 500) lets you debug real production issues in seconds.
learningObjectives: Trace what happens step-by-step from typing a URL to seeing a webpage render
Explain the roles of DNS, IP addresses, ports, and HTTPS encryption (TLS)
Distinguish HTTP methods and status code families (2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx)
commonMistakes: Confusing 401 Unauthorized (not logged in) with 403 Forbidden (logged in, but lacking permission)
Putting sensitive secrets like passwords in URL query parameters instead of HTTPS request bodies

questions.prompt: What job does DNS (Domain Name System) perform when you visit learnpath.org?
options: It translates the human-readable domain name into a numeric IP address
It compiles JavaScript into binary machine code
It stores the website's SQL database tables
It boosts Wi-Fi antenna voltage
questions.correctAnswer: It translates the human-readable domain name into a numeric IP address
questions.explanation: Computers route packets using IP addresses; DNS maps memorable domain names to those IP addresses.

questions.prompt: A server responds with HTTP status code 404. What does the 4xx family indicate?
options: Success — the page loaded
Client-side error — the requested resource could not be found at that path
The server's hard drive caught fire
Permanent redirect to another site
questions.correctAnswer: Client-side error — the requested resource could not be found at that path
questions.explanation: 4xx codes indicate client request errors (400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found), whereas 5xx indicate server failures.

codingChallenge.title: Classify HTTP Status Codes
codingChallenge.instructions: Write a JavaScript function `classifyStatus(code)` that returns `'Success'` for 200-299, `'Redirect'` for 300-399, `'Client Error'` for 400-499, `'Server Error'` for 500-599, and `'Unknown'` otherwise.
codingChallenge.solutionHint: Use `if (code >= 200 && code < 300) return 'Success';` and repeat for 300, 400, and 500 ranges.

moduleTitle: Data Science: Practical Statistics & Decision Analytics
title: Descriptive Statistics: Mean, Median, Variance & Outliers
plainExplanation: Statistics is the art of summarizing thousands of messy numbers into clear truth without being fooled by extremes. Imagine 9 students earn $20/hour and 1 billionaire walks into the room: the average (Mean) jumps sky-high, while the middle value (Median) stays $20/hour and tells the honest story.
whyItMatters: Data scientists, product analysts, and ML engineers use distributions, medians, and variance every day to evaluate A/B tests, detect anomalies, and avoid misleading business decisions.
learningObjectives: Know when Median beats Mean (skewed data and outliers)
Measure data spread using Range and Standard Deviation
Distinguish correlation (moving together) from causation (one causes the other)
commonMistakes: Reporting only the arithmetic mean on heavily skewed data like salaries or website latency
Claiming X causes Y merely because X and Y appear correlated on a chart

questions.prompt: A small startup has salaries: $60k, $62k, $65k, $68k, and $950k (CEO). Which metric best represents a typical employee salary?
options: Median ($65k), because it is resistant to extreme outliers
Mean ($241k), because it includes everyone equally
Maximum ($950k)
Range ($890k)
questions.correctAnswer: Median ($65k), because it is resistant to extreme outliers
questions.explanation: A single huge outlier pulls the arithmetic mean far away from the majority of values; the median stays centered.

questions.prompt: Ice cream sales and sunburn cases both rise every July. What is the correct statistical conclusion?
options: Eating ice cream causes sunburn
They are correlated because of a confounding variable (hot sunny summer weather)
Sunburn makes people buy ice cream
Statistics cannot measure summer weather
questions.correctAnswer: They are correlated because of a confounding variable (hot sunny summer weather)
questions.explanation: Correlation does not imply causation. A third hidden factor (summer sun) drives both variables.

codingChallenge.title: Compute the Median of a Numeric Dataset
codingChallenge.instructions: Write a JavaScript function `calcMedian(nums)` that returns the median of a non-empty array of numbers without mutating the input array. For even lengths, return the average of the two middle numbers.

visibleTests.description: Odd count returns middle sorted value
Even count averages the two middle values

codingChallenge.solutionHint: Sort numerically with `[...nums].sort((a, b) => a - b)`. Check `mid = Math.floor(sorted.length / 2)`.

title: Authentication, Hashing, Encryption & The CIA Triad
plainExplanation: Cybersecurity protects systems around three pillars called the CIA Triad: Confidentiality (only authorized eyes see private data), Integrity (data is not secretly tampered with), and Availability (the service stays online when needed). Passwords are never stored in plain text — we scramble them one-way with salted cryptographic hashes like bcrypt.
whyItMatters: One weak password table or unvalidated input can expose millions of users. Every engineer — whether web, mobile, cloud, or AI — must understand secure authentication and defensive coding from day one.
learningObjectives: Explain Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA Triad) with real examples
Distinguish one-way Hashing (passwords) from two-way Encryption (HTTPS/secrets)
Prevent SQL Injection and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) using parameterized queries and escaping
commonMistakes: Confusing Base64 encoding with encryption (Base64 provides zero security; anyone can decode it instantly)
Building SQL queries by gluing user strings together instead of using parameterized bindings

resources.title: OWASP Top 10 Web Application Security Risks

questions.prompt: Why do secure systems store salted password hashes instead of encrypted passwords?
options: Hashing is one-way so even if the database leaks, attackers cannot decrypt original passwords; salting stops rainbow-table lookups
Hashes take less typing for users
Encryption does not work on text
Browsers require plain text hashes in URLs
questions.correctAnswer: Hashing is one-way so even if the database leaks, attackers cannot decrypt original passwords; salting stops rainbow-table lookups
questions.explanation: A strong password hash (bcrypt/Argon2) cannot be reversed, and a unique random salt guarantees identical passwords produce completely different hashes.

questions.prompt: What is the primary defense against SQL Injection attacks?
options: Using parameterized queries (prepared statements) so user input is strictly treated as data, never executable SQL
Renaming database tables to random letters
Hiding the HTML form with CSS
Asking users politely not to type quotes
questions.correctAnswer: Using parameterized queries (prepared statements) so user input is strictly treated as data, never executable SQL
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries separate SQL code structure from user data bindings at the database driver level.

codingChallenge.title: HTML Escape Utility (XSS Defense)
codingChallenge.instructions: Write a JavaScript function `escapeHtml(text)` that safely escapes `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, and `'` into `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, and `'` respectively.
codingChallenge.solutionHint: Replace `&` FIRST (so you don't double-escape other entities), then `<`, `>`, `"`, and `'`.

title: Docker Containers, Images & Reproducible Deployments
plainExplanation: Have you ever heard a programmer say 'It works on my laptop!' while it crashes on a server? Docker solves this using shipping containers for software. A Dockerfile is the blueprint, an Image is the frozen snapshot containing your code + exact runtime version, and a Container is a running isolated instance of that image anywhere on earth.
whyItMatters: Containers and automated CI/CD pipelines power modern cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes). They guarantee your app runs identically on your laptop, in automated tests, and in production.
learningObjectives: Distinguish a Dockerfile (recipe), Docker Image (template), and Container (running instance)
Explain why containers start in seconds compared to heavy Virtual Machines
Understand CI/CD pipelines: automated lint, test, build, and zero-downtime deploy
commonMistakes: Baking secret API keys directly into a Dockerfile image layer instead of injecting environment variables at runtime
Storing permanent database files inside an ephemeral container without a persistent volume

questions.prompt: Why should you NEVER hardcode production API secrets inside a Dockerfile?
options: Anyone with access to the built image or registry can inspect the layers and steal the secrets
Dockerfiles cannot read letters or numbers
Secrets make Docker images run slower
Linux does not support environment variables
questions.correctAnswer: Anyone with access to the built image or registry can inspect the layers and steal the secrets
questions.explanation: Image layers are cached and portable; secrets should always be injected at runtime via environment variables or a secret manager.

questions.prompt: What does CI (Continuous Integration) automatically do when a developer pushes code?
options: Runs automated builds, linters, and tests to catch regressions before merging
Manually emails every user
Deletes the Git commit history
Buys new server hardware
questions.correctAnswer: Runs automated builds, linters, and tests to catch regressions before merging
questions.explanation: CI catches broken builds and failing tests immediately on every push or pull request.

codingChallenge.title: CI/CD Pipeline Stage Validator
codingChallenge.instructions: Write a JavaScript function `canDeploy(stages)` where `stages` is an array of `{ name: string, passed: boolean, required: boolean }`. Return `true` only if EVERY stage with `required: true` has `passed: true` (optional stages may fail without blocking deploy).

visibleTests.description: Allows deploy when all required stages pass
Blocks deploy when a required test stage fails
